headline: LITHIUM PEGMATITE BULL'S-EYE: Brunswick Drills 17.7m at 1.10% Li₂O Inside 123m Corridor at Quebec's Anatacau Main
snippet: Brunswick Exploration (TSXV: BRW) released its fourth batch of winter drill results from Anatacau Main, Quebec, hitting 17.7m at 1.10% Li₂O within a 123m zone averaging 0.72% Li₂O — plus among the James Bay's highest-grade cesium intercepts at 11.8m of 1.84% Cs₂O. The mineralized structural corridor now extends over 500m east and remains open; three further drill holes have identified additional pegmatites with assays still pending.

headline: UNCLE SAM GOES DEEP: USA Rare Earth Bags $1.6 Billion in Federal Backing and 10% Government Equity Stake
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) secured a $1.3B Commerce Department senior secured loan plus $277M in direct incentives — in exchange for a 10% government equity stake — making it the most heavily backed domestic rare earth play in U.S. history. Motley Fool examines whether the combination of government support and an Oklahoma magnet manufacturing plant positions USAR as a potential multi-bagger as the U.S. races to build a China-independent rare earth supply chain.

headline: TRUMP KILLS IRAN DEAL: Gold Slides to $4,690 as President Calls Ceasefire Proposal 'Totally Unacceptable'
snippet: Gold fell 0.9% to $4,690/oz Monday morning after President Trump rejected Iran's latest ceasefire proposal, calling it 'totally unacceptable' and dashing last week's peace-deal optimism that briefly pushed gold toward $4,750. Silver held near $80 as markets recalibrated the duration of the 10-week US-Iran conflict, which has been the primary driver of 2026's historic precious metals rally.

headline: COPPER'S ACID TEST: Chile Imports ZERO Chinese Sulfuric Acid in March as Ban Threatens a Fifth of Global Copper Output
snippet: Chinese sulfuric acid exports to Chile collapsed to zero in March 2026 from 151,000 mt in the prior year period after China banned acid exports to protect domestic fertilizer supply amid the Middle East conflict, sending Chilean spot prices up 100% to $380/mt. Chile's SX-EW copper operations — which account for roughly a fifth of global supply — were already down 6% in Q1 output before the full shock hit; some producers now have less than 30 days of acid inventory with no near-term Chinese supply in sight.

headline: ZACATECAS SILVER FIRE: Defiance Drills 356 g/t Ag and 2.15 g/t Au in New Structures at Historic Mexican District
snippet: Defiance Silver (TSXV: DEF) reported new high-grade intercepts from the Zacatecas Project, Mexico, including 1.2m at 356 g/t Ag and 2.15 g/t Au within an 11m envelope grading 125 g/t Ag — results from four holes in a 10,000m program. Multiple additional silver-gold structures have been identified across the historically prolific Zacatecas silver district, with a Mineral Resource Estimate in preparation.

headline: CANADA'S BIGGEST URANIUM BUILD: NexGen's Rook I Breaks Ground This Summer — 30 Million Lb/Yr, 20%+ of Global Supply
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX: NXE) will begin construction at Rook I in northern Saskatchewan this summer following final CNSC regulatory approval, with the Arrow deposit targeting production of up to 30 million lb of uranium oxide per year — more than 20% of current global uranium supply. The company's May 7 Q1 2026 earnings call detailed pending major contract announcements and financing milestones as pre-construction site work gets underway.

headline: GOLD MINER GAP: Feneck Says Record Producer Cash Flows at $4,700 Gold Will Force an M&A Wave — Juniors in the Crosshairs
snippet: Analyst John Feneck told Kitco that gold mining equities are underperforming the metal at $4,700+ gold because institutions remain cautious post the Q1 correction, but the resulting cash flow windfall for senior producers creates ideal conditions for an acquisition wave — with junior and mid-tier operators the most likely targets. He argues the valuation gap between the gold price and gold stock performance is the most compelling asymmetric setup in the sector right now.

headline: SECULAR BULL UNBROKEN: Gold and Silver 'Will Reach New All-Time Highs' Once War Fog Lifts, Market Watchers Say
snippet: Multiple strategists told CNBC that gold and silver's 2026 bull market — which pushed gold to nearly $5,600 in Q1 before correcting — is a pause, not a reversal, with new all-time highs expected once the US-Iran conflict resolves. Central bank buying is running at 585 tonnes per quarter with no sign of slowing; silver, up over 150% in a year, is seen as the higher-leverage play in an eventual resolution rally.

headline: NdPr IN FREE FALL? Rare Earth Magnet Metal Drops 21% in April to $99/kg — Still 88% Above Year Open
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide shed 21% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began — with neodymium at $108.96/kg and praseodymium at $109.60/kg. Despite the pullback, NdPr remains 88% above its January 1 open and well above the cash costs of Western producers like MP Materials and Lynas; the May 2026 market outlook characterizes the decline as profit-taking consolidation rather than a structural reversal.

headline: ZIJIN LOCKS IN AFRICA GOLD: C$5.5 Billion Allied Gold Takeover Tracks to May 29 Close With 99%+ Shareholder Approval
snippet: Allied Gold (TSX: AAUC) confirmed regulatory approvals for Zijin Gold International's C$5.5B all-cash offer at C$44/share are progressing cooperatively toward the May 29 outside closing date, with 99%-plus shareholder support already secured in March. The deal — the largest gold M&A of 2026 — would give Zijin three large open-pit gold mines in Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, and Ethiopia; the company also confirmed all African mine sites are operating normally.
